correctness.rationale: Complete independent enumeration agrees on all 20,651 nonempty faces and the full ten-entry face vector. An exact global Hasse-DAG check traverses all 120,222 incidences and 20,651 vertices after 10,320 matched pairs, leaving exactly one vertex, nine 5-cells and one 6-cell. The signed integral algebraic Morse 6-to-5 boundary, expanded through 933 gradient projection states, is the zero vector in nine coordinates. Consequently the 5-skeleton is a wedge of nine 5-spheres and the remaining 6-cell attaches nullhomotopically by the integral Hurewicz isomorphism in degree five. A separate full mod-two simplicial calculation confirms Betti ranks 9 and 1 in degrees five and six; it is not used for the integral conclusion.

originality.rationale: Full-text Section 2 and methodological passages of Conant–Thistlethwaite establish general hypergraph independence but no Pappus path-hypergraph computation. Deshpande–Singh classify complete multipartite, fully whiskered, path, cycle, and perfect rooted tree graph higher-independence complexes, none including the nonchordal cubic Pappus graph. Direct full-text comparison against the same-graph Pappus matching-complex result shows different simplicial vertices and face condition. Targeted equivalent-formulation and published-finding corpus searches returned neighboring graph/complex statements but no covering theorem. Related mathematical statements were compared by exact graph-complex object and logical implication. Unindexed or otherwise inaccessible equivalent work remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The Pappus graph is a canonical highly symmetric 18-vertex incidence graph and two-independence is its first nontrivial higher-independence condition, equivalently avoidance of induced length-two paths as three-vertex hyperedges. Its complete integral mixed-dimensional homotopy type supplies a natural benchmark beyond known graph-family classifications; the degree-six sphere cannot be inferred from ordinary Pappus matching/independence theorems. The integer attaching-map computation distinguishes a homotopy classification from field Betti numbers.
